content:
34 years ago, Sharon Stone became a sex symbol with her passionate performance in Basic Instinct, and now she says she has chosen a celibate lifestyle.

Stone appeared on Mayim Bialik's podcast "Breakdown" this week for a wide-ranging interview, in which she revealed she has "not been a girlfriend in a very long time," because her recent romantic path has "absolutely gone nowhere."

The Oscar-nominated actress said, "I have been celibate for a considerable period of time," and noted that she "really just want to be with someone I care about now."

Stone's three sons — Roan (26), Laird (21), and Quinn (20) — are all grown up, and she believes her priorities in relationships have changed.

She said, "I want the other person to be my partner, not just a sex partner. I am a bit tired of that kind of relationship. So I'm in this phase right now where it's just 'completely going nowhere,' but I think to get what I really want, I have to be willing to stay in this phase."

Stone divorced journalist Phil Bronstein in 2004 after six years of marriage; their eldest son Roan was born to the couple. Before that, she was married to television and film producer Michael Greenburg from 1984 to 1987.

In 2018, she was reported by the media to be in a relationship with Italian-Swiss actor and producer Angelo Boffa, and the two reportedly split later that same year.

In other parts of the "Breakdown" interview, Stone said she does not think she has "already met the love of her life," and recalled that a psychic once told her she would have to wait until she was "quite old, around seventy" to meet her other half.

The 68-year-old laughed and said, "That's now."

Stone is one of a growing number of celebrities who have publicly spoken about choosing a celibate lifestyle. In 2024, musician Lenny Kravitz revealed he had not had sex for nine years, while actress Julia Fox said the Supreme Court's 2022 decision overturning abortion rights had led her to decide on celibacy.

In February this year, former "Project Runway" mentor Tim Gunn shared on Chelsea Handler's podcast "Dear Chelsea" that he has been celibate for 43 years, since splitting from an unfaithful ex in 1982.

He said this lifestyle helped him adjust to the prolonged self-isolation of the 2020 COVID pandemic: "I was probably one of the few people who truly enjoyed that period."
